And their saying: ﴿and evil is the burden for them on the Day of Resurrection﴾, meaning: evil is the burden they carry on the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 20, verse 102:

As for His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿The Day the Trumpet is blown⁠﴾. Abu 'Amr recited: "And the Day We blow into the Trumpet" (wa-yawma nanfakhu fi al-sur), and he argued from what is conjoined to it in His saying: ﴿And We shall gather the criminals⁠﴾. The rest of the readers recited: ﴿The Day the Trumpet is blown⁠﴾. This is the preferable reading. We have already explained the meaning of al-Sur (the Trumpet) earlier.

As for His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And We shall gather the criminals on that Day, blue-eyed⁠﴾, al-Hasan, Qatadah and a group said: "Blind." If someone says: How can this be consistent, when Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿And you have come to Us alone, as We created you the first time⁠﴾, and Allah the Exalted created them with sight? The answer: it is related from Ibn 'Abbas that on the Day of Resurrection there are stages and states; they are gathered seeing, then they become blind.

The second opinion regarding His saying ﴿zurqan⁠﴾ (blue-eyed): it is the greenness of the eye, so the disbelievers will be gathered with blue eyes and black faces. The third opinion: "thirsty," meaning their eyes have changed from the intensity of thirst. The fourth opinion: ﴿zurqan⁠﴾ means their gazes are fixed from the magnitude of fear. The poet said:

(Your two eyes have turned blue, O son of Mak'abar... Likewise every Dabbi from baseness is blue-eyed.)

The fifth opinion: ﴿zurqan⁠﴾ means one-eyed (ahad al-basar), because the blue-eyed (azraq) is one whose sight is weak.

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 20, verse 103:

And His saying: ﴿They will whisper among themselves﴾ means: they will speak secretly to one another, and they will talk in a low voice.

And His saying: ﴿You did not remain except for ten [days]﴾ means: you did not remain except for ten. Some of them have said: this refers to "the grave," and some have said: it refers to the world. If someone says: this is a plain lie, for they remained in the world and in the grave for many years! The answer to this is: because of the intensity of the horror of the Resurrection, they will think that they did not remain except for this amount. Some of them have said: Allah the Exalted will lift the punishment from them between the two blasts, so they will find rest, and their saying ﴿You did not remain except for ten﴾ refers to this.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 20, verse 104:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿We know best what they will say﴾. Its meaning: I am knowing of what they say, even if they whisper.

And His saying: ﴿When their most exemplary in way says﴾. The Arabs say: "So-and-so is the most exemplary (amthal) of his people," meaning: the most just (a'dal) of his people. The meaning of the verse here is: the most intelligent of them and the best of them in way within himself.

And His saying: ﴿You did not remain except a day﴾. That is: you did not remain except a day.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 20, verse 105:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿They ask you about the mountains.﴾ Al-Hasan al-Basri said: The polytheists asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "What will Allah do with these mountains on the Day of Resurrection?" So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

And His words: ﴿Say: My Lord will blow them away with a blast.﴾ Al-nasf (uprooting, blowing away) is the pulling out from the root. The meaning of al-nasf in the verse is: making the mountains move away (from their places), or turning them into dust (haba'), making them into flowing sand.

Translation:

And His saying: ﴿So He will leave it a level plain, smooth and flat﴾. That is: He will leave the places of the mountains as a level plain (qa'), smooth and flat (safsaf). The qa' is the wide, even place, and the safsaf is the smooth ground in which there is no vegetation.
"And His saying: ﴿You will not see therein any crookedness or any elevation.﴾ That is: hadaba (raised ground) and nabk (uneven hillocks). Its meaning: a lowering and a raising."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 20, verse 108:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿On that Day they will follow the summoner, there being no deviation from him﴾. The people of tafsir said: "The summoner here is Israfil (the angel of the Trumpet), who places the Trumpet (al-sur) to his mouth and says: 'O decayed bones, torn skins, and scattered flesh, come forth to the presentation before the Most Merciful'" — or words to this effect.

And His saying: ﴿there being no deviation from him﴾, meaning: they will not turn aside to the right or to the left. It was also said: they will be unable not to follow him.

And His saying: ﴿And voices will be hushed before the Most Merciful﴾, meaning: they will be stilled and humbled. Qatadah said: "They will be humbled." The poet said:

((So when the news of al-Zubair came, the walls of al-Madinah were shaken, and the mountains humbled (al-khushu')).

And His saying: ﴿so you will hear nothing but a whisper (hamsan)﴾. The hams is the hidden sound. It is said: the sound of footsteps is like the hams of camels. The poet said:

(So they spent the night slaughtering, while one who sees clearly in the darkness, lean and hurrying (hams), traveled on.)

On that Day, intercession will not benefit anyone, meaning: intercession will not benefit anyone.

And His saying: "except for one whom the Most Merciful has permitted," meaning: except for one for whom the Most Merciful has permitted intercession.

And His saying: "and whose word He approves," meaning: the word "There is no god but Allah," which is the word approved by Allah.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 20, verse 110:

The words of the Most High: ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them﴾, meaning: He knows what is before them of the Hereafter, and what is behind them of their deeds. It is also said: "He knows what is before them" meaning: (He did not create them while He intends to create them).

And His words: ﴿and what is behind them﴾, meaning: those who came after them, from those who preceded them and whom they succeeded.

And His words: ﴿but they cannot encompass Him in knowledge﴾, meaning: they cannot encompass Allah in knowledge. Allah encompasses things, and He is not encompassed; for ihatah (encompassment, comprehensive knowledge) of a thing is knowledge of the thing from every aspect that can be known, and Allah the Most High is not measured by anyone's measure, nor does anyone reach the full reality of His greatness. As for all other things, Allah knows every thing from every aspect in which it can be known.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 20, verse 111:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all.﴾ Meaning: the faces will be abased. Ṭalq ibn Abī Ḥabīb said: "The faces will fall down (in prostration)."

And His saying: ﴿the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all﴾ refers to the One who is Everlasting, who has never ceased to be. Al-Qayyum is the One who stands in charge of the creation's management, and who stands over every soul for what it has earned.

And His saying: ﴿And he has indeed failed who carries injustice.﴾ Meaning: he who carries polytheism is ruined, and "carrying polytheism" is itself the act of associating partners with God.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 20, verse 112:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer﴾ — the meaning is apparent.

And His words: ﴿so he will not fear injustice or diminution﴾ — His words ﴿injustice﴾ mean: that the sin of another be placed upon him. ﴿Nor diminution﴾ means: he will not fear that anything of his due right be reduced. It was also said: ﴿injustice﴾ means: that his obedience not be accepted, and ﴿diminution﴾ means: that some of his reward be reduced.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 20, verse 113:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And thus We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an﴾, meaning: in the tongue of the Arabs. And His saying: ﴿and We have varied in it some of the threats﴾, meaning: We have varied the discourse in it by mentioning the threat (wa'id). Qatadah said: it is the mention of the events of Allah among the earlier nations.

And His saying: ﴿so that they may fear Allah﴾, meaning: that they may avoid shirk and sins.

And His saying: ﴿or it may produce for them a remembrance﴾, meaning: the Qur'an produces for them consideration (i'tibar), so that they take heed by it. Some of them said: the threat produces for them a mention of the punishment, so that they refrain from sins. Some of them said: ﴿or it may produce for them a remembrance﴾ means: honour for them through their faith in it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 20, verse 114:

His saying, Exalted be Allah, the King, the Truth (﴿Fa-ta'ala Allahu al-Malik al-Haqq﴾): He is exalted, the King, the True, the Possessor of truth.

And His saying: ﴿And do not hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation to you is completed﴾. Concerning it there are several views. The best known is what Ibn 'Abbas and others have related: that when Jibril came down to the Prophet with the Qur'an, the Prophet would recite the beginning of the verse before Jibril had finished conveying it, out of fear of forgetting it and losing it. So Allah, Exalted is He, revealed this verse. Its meaning: do not hasten to recite the Qur'an before Jibril has finished conveying it. The second view: its meaning is, do not seek the descent (of revelation) from Allah, Exalted is He, but be patient until Jibril comes to you with what Allah, Exalted is He, sends down. The third view: its meaning is, do not explain to people what has not yet been made clear to you in its interpretation; that is, do not explain on your own authority. The first view is the well-known one.

And His saying: ﴿And say: My Lord, increase me in knowledge﴾. That is, knowledge beyond what you have learned. When Ibn Mas'ud recited this verse, he would say: "O Allah, increase me in faith and certainty." It is related from Malik ibn Anas that he said: "It is the nature of the son of Adam not to know everything, and it is the nature of the son of Adam to know and then forget, and it is the nature of the son of Adam to seek from Allah knowledge beyond his own knowledge."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 20, verse 115:

The Almighty's saying: ﴿And We had already made a covenant with Adam before, but he forgot﴾. Here "al-'ahd" (covenant) means "al-amr" (the command).

And His saying: ﴿but he forgot﴾ means: he neglected. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that man was called insan (human) because he forgets (yansa).

And His saying: ﴿and We found in him no resolve﴾ means: patience. It was also said: firmness of judgment. 'Atiyyah said: [it means] preserving what he was commanded. Al-'azm (resolve) is the settling of the soul upon the act.

It is related from al-Hasan al-Basri that he said: "If the intellect of Adam were weighed against the intellect of all his descendants, it would outweigh them, and Allah the Almighty has said: ﴿and We found in him no resolve﴾." It is related from Abu Umamah al-Bahili that he said: "If the forbearance of Adam were weighed against the forbearance of all his descendants, his forbearance would outweigh theirs, and Allah the Almighty has said: ﴿and We found in him no resolve﴾."

If it is said: Do you say that Adam (peace be upon him) was forgetful of the command of Allah the Almighty when he ate from the tree? We say: It is possible that he forgot. Some of them said: he forgot the punishment of Allah the Almighty, and he thought that it was a prohibition of disapproval (nahy tanzih), not a prohibition of prohibition (nahy tahrim). Others said: he thought that he had only been forbidden a specific tree, and had not been forbidden the whole category of trees.
His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," so they prostrated, except Iblis; he refused.﴾ Its meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 20, verse 117:

And His saying: ﴿So We said, "O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and to your wife, so let him not drive you both out of the Garden and [thus] you will suffer."﴾ That is: you will be wearied and toil. Al-Suddi said: [the suffering is] through tilling, reaping, grinding and baking. It is related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr that God, exalted is He, sent down to him a red bull, and he began to plough, with sweat dripping from his forehead, and that is his suffering. It is also related from Sa'id that he said: Adam began driving the bull, and he had become weary and was sweating, so he said, "O Hawwa', this is from your side," and that remained in his offspring until the Day of Resurrection, so they say at the time of ploughing: "Hawhaw" (ḥawḥaw). This was mentioned by Ibn Faris in his tafsir.

Abu al-Husayn ibn Faris said in his tafsir: And upon this is the well-known report related by Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Adam met Musa, peace be upon them both, and [Musa] said: 'O Adam, you are the one who made us wretched and expelled us from the Garden.' Adam said to him: 'O Musa, do you blame me for a matter that Allah decreed for me before I was created?' ... the report in full," until he said: "So Adam won the argument against Musa three times."

In some hadith it is said: when God, exalted is He, sent Adam down to the earth, He said: "I will feed you until your forehead sweats and your body grows weary," and this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿...you will suffer.﴾

If someone says: Why did He not say "you two will suffer" (fa-tashqayā), when He had already said before: ﴿so let him not drive you both out⦆?

The answer is in two respects. First: its meaning is "you two will suffer," but He sufficed with mentioning one of them instead of the other. A parallel to this is His exalted saying: ﴿[sitting] on the right and on the left, a sitter﴾, meaning "two sitters."

Second: He said ﴿you will suffer﴾ (fa-tashqā) because he is the one who earns and strives for the woman, so the toil falls upon him.
"Indeed, for you there is that you will not hunger therein, nor be left naked." The apparent meaning is clear.

And His saying: ﴿And that you will not thirst therein, nor be exposed to the sun﴾. That is: you will not be thirsty, and the harm of the sun will not reach you. If it is said: there is no sun in Paradise, so how does this statement stand? The answer: it stands, because the people of Paradise are in extended shade, so the harm of the sun does not reach them as it reaches them in this world. It was also said that its meaning is: no heat will reach you to harm you, and "nor be exposed to the sun" means: you will not sweat. The Arabs say: "adha (he was exposed to the sun) when he came forward into the sun." In some reports: "Come out into the sun (idha) for the one you have served." ʿUmar ibn Abi Rabiʿa al-Makhzumi, Abu al-Khattab, who was born on the night ʿUmar died, may Allah be pleased with him, said:

(She saw a man: as for when the sun confronts him, he is exposed to it, and as for the evening, he is sheltered.)

Almighty Allah's saying: ﴿Then Satan whispered to him, saying, "O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?"﴾ That is, one that does not wear out and does not perish. We have already explained the meaning of the "tree of eternity" (shajarat al-khuld) earlier.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 20, verse 121:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So they both ate from it, and their private parts became apparent to them﴾, meaning: their awrat (private parts). Some of the scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: their private parts became apparent to them alone, and not to others, because God, may He be exalted, said: ﴿and their private parts became apparent to them﴾.

And His saying: ﴿and they began to cover themselves﴾, meaning: they began (talaba). It is said: "taffaqa yaf'alu kadha" (tafiqa yaf'alu kadhā, "he began to do such-and-such") when he starts doing it.

And His saying: ﴿yakhsifan﴾, meaning: they stuck the leaves to the leaves to cover themselves.

And His saying: ﴿over themselves from the leaves of the Garden﴾, meaning: to cover themselves.

And His saying: ﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord﴾. Ibn Qutaybah said: it is permissible to say "Adam disobeyed" ('asa Adam), but it is not said "Adam is disobedient" ('ass), because the word "'asin" (disobedient) is only used when a person habitually commits disobedience. This is like a man who sews his garment: one says "he sewed his garment" (khāta thawbahu), but one does not say "khayyat" (tailor) unless he has made sewing a habit.

As for His saying: ﴿and he went astray﴾, its meaning: he strayed and failed. The straying here means: he erred from the path of truth, and the failure (khaybah) is: the loss of what he hoped for regarding eternity.

Ibn al-A'rabi said: "ghawa" means his life was spoiled, and he passed from honour to humiliation, and from ease to hardship.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Then his Lord chose him, accepted his repentance, and guided him﴾. That is: his Lord chose him (ikhtarah), and turned to him in forgiveness, that is, accepted his repentance. "And guided him" means: He directed him to turning back (to Allah) in repentance (al-inabah).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 20, verse 123:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said: Go down from it, all of you, some of you enemies to others.﴾ And we have explained this before.

And His saying: ﴿So when guidance comes to you from Me﴾ meaning: a clarification.

And His saying: ﴿Whoever follows My guidance will not go astray, nor will he suffer.﴾ Meaning: he will not go astray in this world, nor will he suffer in the Hereafter. It is narrated from al-Sha'bi (may Allah have mercy on him) that he said: Allah, exalted is He, protects whoever follows the Qur'an and acts by what is in it from going astray or suffering, and then he recited this verse.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 20, verse 124:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And whoever turns away from My remembrance﴾ means: from My revelation.

And His saying: ﴿then indeed for him is a constricted life﴾ — concerning it there are several opinions.

It is related from Ibn Mas'ud, Abu Hurayrah and Abu Sa'id al-Khudri that they said: it is the punishment of the grave. Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "He is squeezed until his ribs are interlocked." In some musnads this is related from the Prophet (ﷺ), and its wording is: "The grave closes in upon him until his ribs are interlocked, and it remains so until he is resurrected." He said this concerning this verse.

The second opinion: al-Dahhak said: it is the consuming of what is forbidden (haram). Some others said: it is that he earns less than what suffices him. And al-Dank (ḍank) is the narrowness. Al-Hasan said: "a constricted life" is the punishment of Hell. Some others said: it is al-Dari' (a thorny plant of Hell), and al-Zaqqum (within the Fire).

And His saying: ﴿And We will raise him up blind on the Day of Resurrection﴾ — he said: blind to the proof. It is also said: blind in the eye. We have already mentioned that it is related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: He will gather them seeing, then they will become blind. It was also said: blind to the truth, and it was said: blind to everything except the punishment of Hell.

"The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿He will say: My Lord, why have You raised me blind, when I was seeing?﴾ Its meaning: why have You raised me blind to the proof, when I was seeing [with insight] into the proof? And it is said: blind in the eye, when I was sharp of sight."

The Almighty said: ﴿He said, "Thus did Our signs come to you, and you forgot them."﴾ That is, you abandoned them.

And His saying: ﴿So likewise today you are forgotten.﴾ That is, you are abandoned. Qatadah said: "They forgot the good, but they did not forget the punishment."

Almighty God's words: ﴿And thus do We recompense those who transgress﴾ means: those who associate partners with God (shirk).

His words: ﴿and do not believe in the signs of their Lord﴾ — the meaning is apparent.

His words: ﴿And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more lasting﴾. That is: greater and more enduring.

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 20, verse 128:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Has it not become clear to them﴾. It is also read "nahdi" with the letter nun. So His words ﴿yahdi﴾ with the letter ya' mean: it guides, i.e. the Qur'an guides. And the meaning of "nahdi" is: we make clear (nubayyin). His words "nahdi" mean: we ourselves make clear, and its connection with the particle lam is evidence that it carries the meaning of making clear (al-tabayyun).

His words: ﴿How many generations We destroyed before them, in whose dwellings they walk﴾. The people of tafsir said: this address is to the Quraysh, who used to travel to al-Sham, and they would see the dwellings of those who were destroyed, such as the companions of al-Hijr, Thamud, and the towns of Lut.

His words: ﴿Indeed in that are signs﴾ meaning: indeed they are indications and lessons.

His words: ﴿for people of understanding (ulī al-nuhā)﴾ meaning: for people of intellect. It is said: so-and-so is dhu nuhyah, meaning: possessor of intellect.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 20, verse 129:

The Almighty's saying: ﴿And had it not been for a word that had already preceded from your Lord﴾ contains a inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in its order, and its meaning is: "And had it not been for a word that had already preceded from your Lord, and a specified term (ajal musamma), ﴿it would have been inevitable (lizaman)﴾," meaning the punishment would have been inevitable. The "word" is the decree to postpone the punishment, and the "specified term" is the promise of the Resurrection. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Nay, the Hour is their appointed time, and the Hour is more calamitous and more bitter.﴾

As for the Almighty's saying: ﴿lizaman﴾, it means the punishment will not part from them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 20, verse 130:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So be patient over what they say, and glorify the praise of your Lord﴾. That is: pray, by the command of your Lord.

And His saying: ﴿before the rising of the sun﴾ is the Fajr (dawn prayer). ﴿And before its setting﴾ is the 'Asr (afternoon prayer). ﴿And during the hours of the night﴾ is the Maghrib (sunset prayer) and the 'Isha' (night prayer). Al-ana' is the plural of ini, and al-ini means the hour.

And His saying: ﴿and the extremities of the day﴾ is the Zuhr (noon prayer). If it is asked: how are they called the extremities of the day? We say: because the end of the first half of the day is its extremity and the beginning of the second half is its extremity. This is the saying of Qatadah and most of the exegetes. Some of them said: the extremities of the day are the hours of the day for voluntary prayer, and according to this His saying "before the setting of the sun" includes Zuhr and 'Asr. Some others said: the extremities of the day intended by it are Subh (dawn) and 'Asr, and it is mentioned to emphasise what has preceded. It has been established by the narration of Jarir ibn 'Abd Allah al-Bajali, who said: "We were sitting with the Prophet (ﷺ), and he looked at the moon on the night of the full moon and said: 'Indeed you will see your Lord just as you see this, and he pointed to the moon, you will not be hindered in seeing Him. So if you are able not to be overcome in a prayer before the rising of the sun and before its setting, then do so.' Then he recited this verse: ﴿So glorify the praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting﴾."

The Shaykh, the Imam, said: This was related to us by al-Makki ibn 'Abd al-Razzaq, who said: my grandfather Abu al-Haytham related to us, who said: al-Firabri related to us, who said: al-Bukhari, may Allah be pleased with him, related to us, who said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim related to us, from Jarir ibn 'Abd al-Hamid al-Dabbi, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, from Jarir... [the hadith].

His saying: ﴿so that you may be content﴾ means: so that you may be content with His reward. It has also been read as "la'allaka tur-da" in the passive form, meaning: so that you may be given His reward.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 20, verse 131:

The Exalted's saying: ﴿And do not extend your eyes toward that which We have bestowed upon pairs of them﴾. It is narrated from Abu Rafi' that the Prophet (ﷺ) had a guest arrive, and he had nothing to offer. So he sent to a Jew to borrow food from him, but the Jew refused except against a pledge. So he pledged his armour to him, and then God Most High revealed this verse.

His saying: ﴿pairs of them﴾, i.e., men. It was also said: guests from among them.

His saying: ﴿the splendour of the life of this world﴾. (The adornment of the life of this world; it was also said: the splendour of the life of this world) its radiance and beauty, and that which pleases the beholder of them both.

His saying: ﴿that We may test them thereby﴾, i.e., We may cause them to fall into trial because of it.

His saying: ﴿But the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting﴾, i.e., better for you in the Hereafter, and more lasting in blessing in this world.

It is narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b that he said: Whoever does not find consolation in the might of God Most High, his soul will be cut to pieces by regrets, and whoever follows with his gaze what is in the hands of people, his grief will be prolonged, and whoever thinks that the blessing of God Most High lies in his food, his drink and his clothing, his deeds have become few and his punishment has drawn near.

And from Yazid ibn Maysarah, who said: They used to call this world "the sow," and had they known a name more vile than it, they would have named it by it. So whenever it came toward one of them, he would say: "Away from me, O sow!"

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 20, verse 132:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And enjoin prayer upon your family, and be steadfast in it.﴾ Regarding His saying ﴿your family﴾ there are two opinions: the first is the people of your religion (ahl dinik), and the second is your kinsfolk and your people.

In some musnad collections, it is related from Salman al-Farisi, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet, when something good befell his family, would order them to pray, and he would recite this verse: ﴿And enjoin prayer upon your family, and be steadfast in it.﴾

As for His saying ﴿We do not ask you for provision﴾, meaning: We do not ask you to provide sustenance for anyone of My creation, nor to provide sustenance for yourself. It was also said: (it means) reward.

As for His saying ﴿We provide for you﴾, meaning: We deliver your provision to you. It was also said: We bring you into being.

As for His saying ﴿And the final outcome is for taqwa﴾, meaning: (for the people of) taqwa (God-consciousness).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 20, verse 133:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they say, "Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?"﴾ That is, the sign they proposed, for he had already brought them many signs.

And His saying: ﴿Has there not come to them clear evidence of what is in the former scriptures?﴾ That is, a clarification of what is in the former scriptures concerning the news of the nations. For they proposed signs, and were given them, yet did not believe, so God, exalted is He, destroyed them. And if We were to give these people [signs] as well, and they did not believe, We would bring about their destruction too.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 20, verse 134:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before it﴾, meaning: before the sending of the Messengers and the sending down of the Qur'an.

His saying: ﴿they would have said, "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger?"﴾, meaning: they would have said on the Day of Resurrection.

And His saying: ﴿so that we would have followed Your signs before we were humiliated and disgraced﴾, meaning: humiliated in this world and disgraced in the Hereafter. Dhull (humiliation) is abasement, and khizy (disgrace) is exposure.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 20, verse 135:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: Each one is waiting, so wait.﴾ It is related that the polytheists said: "We are waiting for Muhammad to be struck by the calamities of time; when he dies, we will be rid of him." So Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse: ﴿Say: Each one is waiting﴾, meaning: awaiting (muntazir).

And His saying: ﴿so wait﴾, meaning: then await.

And His saying: ﴿So you will come to know who are the people of the even path﴾. In the irregular reading (al-shadh, i.e. a non-canonical reading) it is "min ashab al-sirat al-sawa" on the pattern fu'la, while the well-known reading is "al-sawi". The meaning of "al-sirat al-sawi" is the upright religion (al-din al-qayyim).

And His saying: ﴿and who is rightly guided﴾, meaning: who has been guided and set on right course. "Are the ones who are rightly guided we, or you?"
